questions.question: Supervisor is still cycling — how should I proceed?

options.label: Stop the bleed: bootout supervisor (Recommended)
options.description: `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.claudio1.claude-remote-control`. Children get TERM, deregister cleanly, phantoms stop accumulating. We can then debug the supervisor at our pace without it eating cloud quota.

options.label: Add instrumentation and watch one tick
options.description: Patch supervisor.py to log `wanted=...` and `running=...` per tick, restart it, and capture one full cycle so we can see exactly which name disappears from `wanted`. Leaves it cycling while we look.

options.label: Just leave it — it's not actively harmful
options.description: Phantoms age out; spawn rate is bounded by tick interval. Stop investigating and move on.

transcript_tail.text: we also have too many dirs

Two separate concerns now — let me address the dirs question and keep going on the supervisor flap (they're independent).

**On the dirs:** the supervisor doesn't spawn from `~/dev` listing — it spawns from `~/.ai-harness/active-dirs.txt`, which is exactly 6 entries (`dev FamilyFund ai-harness dstrader dstrader-docker job-search`). Extra dirs like `ai-harness-public`, `ai-harness-private`, `ai-harness-host-defaults`, `*-worktrees`, `*-secrets` are silently filtered out — they're not causing extra servers. They are clutter, though. Many are likely the artifacts of the 2026-05-26 public/private swap, the worktree convention, and your secrets layout. We can audit them in a follow-up — but they aren't what's behind the picker explosion.

**The actual cause** is in [logs/manager.log](logs/manager.log) — the supervisor is in a full deactivate→respawn cycle every ~60s for ALL 6 servers:

```
21:34:09 deactivate: mm-dev not in allowlist (pid 89320)
21:34:20 start:      mm-dev
21:34:31 deactivate: mm-dstrader-docker not in allowlist (pid 89328)
21:34:52 start:      mm-dstrader-docker
21:35:14 deactivate: mm-FamilyFund not in allowlist (pid 89726)
21:35:24 start:      mm-FamilyFund
...
```

So on tick N the supervisor spawns `mm-dstrader-docker`, on tick N+1 it considers the freshly-spawned process "not in allowlist" and kills it. Every kill leaves a phantom cloud registration → that's where your 15 picker entries came from.

Let me check `discover()` to see why a name is in `wanted` one tick but not the next.

You're right — the spawn itself is succeeding (each child connects, gets a real `env_01...`, says "Ready"). It's the supervisor's decision that they're "not in allowlist" that's the lie — and *that* lie is what's killing & respawning them, leaving cloud phantoms.

Let me confirm by looking at `_allowlist()` and check for a read race / second supervisor.

🎯 **Found the actual bug.** Look at this:

```
$ ps -axo command | grep -oE "/claude\s+remote-control\s+--name\s+mm-\S+"
/claude remote-control --name mm-FamilyFund
/claude remote-control --name mm-ai-harness
/claude remote-control --name mm-dev
```

Only **3 of 5** running children show up. The supervisor's `running_servers()` regex needs `/claude remote-control --name mm-XXX` — but `ps -axo command` **truncates the command line** on macOS, hiding `--name` for many of them. Let me confirm:

OK — you were right that I was framing this wrong. The spawn isn't failing; the children are connecting cleanly. The real issue is the supervisor's **reconcile loop incorrectly killing live servers** every ~30s because something in its decision-making is wrong (not a spawn problem — a "wanted set" problem). My CLI dry-run of `discover()` returned all 6 servers consistently, so the bug is somewhere between what `discover()` returns and what the running supervisor's `wanted` set contains at tick time.

Until I find that, the supervisor is burning cloud registrations every cycle. Let me update tasks and ask you how you want to proceed, because at this point I'd rather pause the supervisor than keep poking from the outside.
